_meta.status: DRAFT — written by Claude from the pack's code (lambda/validator/vat_rules/de.py); not yet human-reviewed

kinds.missing: every target must be present and is absent
kinds.missing-any: at least one of the targets must be present; none is. When the targets carry a `group`, at least one per group must be present ("the seller's VAT ID or tax number, and the buyer's VAT ID"); a field result keeps its group
kinds.invalid: the target is present but its value is wrong (format, code list, checksum)
kinds.forbidden: the target is present but not allowed in this combination
kinds.inconsistent: the fields disagree. In a calculation the result is the target (it is what the rule checks, and recomputing it always satisfies the rule) and the inputs are operands; in a comparison with no derived side (dates, codes that must match), every field is an operand
kinds.structural: the XML breaks a rule the simplified JSON cannot express (a duplicated, empty or malformed element). Any sender's invoice can trip it; our own generator never should, so `generator` says why and a hit on a document we generated is a bug. Fields point at the nearest data
kinds.unrepresentable: concerns XRechnung-extension structures the simplified JSON has no fields for; the note has to carry the whole message

_meta.anchored: a field with "anchored": true applies only on the anchor's branch: it keeps the matches the anchor is, lies inside, or contains (the document itself excepted); a containing anchor must supply every ~. index, or it would widen to every item. For a rule that fires on different kinds of object, each target names its own

roles.condition: a field whose value made the rule apply
roles.operand: an input of a calculation, or one side of a comparison with no derived side

conventions.no rule-set conditions: BT-24 (and anything else that only selects which rule set runs, e.g. $isCVD) is never a condition: every rule in the set already presupposes it
conventions.narrowest field: map the field the rule tests, not its group; the group is a path prefix any consumer can walk up to. Map a group only when its entries are what is tested ("exactly one entry such that …"), and then with a filter
conventions.schema, not generator: fields name what the simplified-JSON schema can hold; what an editor shows of them is a UX question
conventions.anchor: `anchor` accepts what check_anchors.py reports for the rule (a collision, an unbound ~., a relative path off the schema), and says why it does no harm
conventions.notes: `note` is shown to the person checking the invoice, whoever sent it: plain words, no BT codes. `generator` says why our own generator can't (or rarely does) trip the rule; `remark` is for whoever maintains this table. Neither is shown

paths.syntax: JSON Pointer patterns (@facturion/pointer-patterns, SPEC.md): a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) is a pattern matching itself
the list index of the finding's anchor at this position; no anchor there → every item
paths.~*: every item, regardless of the anchor
paths.~?f=v: the entries whose member f equals 'v'; none matching → the list itself, as the place to add one
paths.~?f!=v: the entries whose member f is a string other than 'v'; none matching → nothing
paths.~?a~1b=v: a nested member: the entries whose a/b equals 'v' (~1 separates the steps)
paths.~?!f: the entries without member f (missing or null; an empty string counts as present); none → nothing
paths.unmatched filters: only a target's unmatched ~?f=v means "add one here"; a condition's or operand's yields nothing
paths.0/x: relative to the finding's anchor (Relative JSON Pointer; 0 = the anchor itself)

_meta.anchors: pack findings carry no location, so no anchor: every path is absolute

FCT-VAT-DE-01.remark: The check accepts the seller's own VAT ID or tax number only; a tax representative's VAT ID doesn't count (unlike BR-S-02).

FCT-VAT-DE-02.note: Only a warning. German VAT law requires reverse-charge invoices to say so ("Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers", or the English "reverse charge"). Add it as an invoice note, or as the exemption reason of the reverse-charge VAT entry.
FCT-VAT-DE-02.remark: The check searches all notes and every breakdown entry's reason (_exemption_haystack); the AE entry's reason is the natural place, /notes the alternative (a target list: add a note).

FCT-VAT-DE-04.note: Only a hint. The invoice charges no VAT and the seller has no VAT ID, which looks like a small business under §19 UStG (Kleinunternehmer). If it is one, the invoice must say so in a note or exemption reason; if it isn't, the VAT is missing.
FCT-VAT-DE-04.remark: Fires when every line's rate is 0 or absent, there's no seller VAT ID and no Kleinunternehmer wording in notes or breakdown reasons.

FCT-VAT-DE-05.note: Only a warning. German VAT law requires the date of supply: a delivery date, a service period, or a VAT point date. If the supply date is the invoice date, say so in a note ("Leistungsdatum entspricht Rechnungsdatum").
FCT-VAT-DE-05.remark: The period counts only with both dates; line periods don't count (unlike BR-DE-TMP-32).

FCT-VAT-DE-06.remark: Fires once for both parties; each absent field among the eight is what's missing (the message lists them).

FCT-VAT-DE-07.note: Only a warning. An intra-community supply must say that it is exempt ("steuerfreie innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung", or "exempt intra-community supply"). Add it as an invoice note, or as the exemption reason of that VAT entry.
FCT-VAT-DE-07.remark: Fires only when seller and buyer countries differ (the cross-border precondition); FCT-VAT-DE-08 covers the same-country case.

FCT-VAT-DE-08.note: Only a hint. The invoice is marked as an intra-community supply, but seller and buyer are in the same country. Either the VAT category or one of the addresses is wrong.
